Originally from Taiwan, now based in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania.

I’m a PhD researcher in Civil and Environmental Engineering at Lehigh University. My work sits at the intersection of behavioral science, LLM-based simulation, and quantitative evaluation. A central part of my research is understanding and modeling human decision-making. I evaluate whether LLMs capture meaningful decision processes, not only whether their answers sound plausible, but whether their perceptions and constraints relate coherently to the choices they make. I also work with agent-based modeling, which is widely used to simulate how individual decisions accumulate over time and interact with larger social, financial, and physical systems. Portfolio · LinkedIn · Email

Current focus: MCP-based network operations with UniFi MCP Server, and Noesis — a governed multi-agent system and the Ansible code that deploys it.

Featured Projects

UniFi MCP Server

An open-source Model Context Protocol server that gives AI agents one standard interface to UniFi infrastructure: UniFi Network, UniFi Protect, and the UniFi cloud APIs. Agents can inspect clients, devices, firewall policy, and sites, and can change configuration when the operator allows it.

  • 290+ GitHub stars, and an active community that contributes code, reports bugs, and requests features.
  • Built-in safety controls: every write needs explicit confirmation and supports a dry-run preview. Read-only and dry-run server modes and role-based risk tiers limit what an agent can do, and a hash-chained audit log records each change.
  • Flexible deployment: a PyPI package or multi-architecture container over stdio or Streamable HTTP, with Ansible and Helm options and an optional multi-controller fleet mode.

Python · FastMCP · Pydantic · Apache-2.0

Repository · Tool reference · Contributing guide · Discussions

Noesis Agent Stack

A governed multi-agent system built on Hermes Agent profiles. A central orchestrator plans work, gives each task to the specialist with the narrowest mandate, and combines the results. The orchestrator itself has no execution access.

  • Durable handoffs: work moves as typed task contracts in an append-only ledger, not as chat history.
  • Approval boundaries: irreversible operations wait at a human approval gate, and reviewer-only profiles audit work they did not do.

Status: the orchestration control plane passes its repository test suite. Production activation is phase-gated and not yet complete; the repository's status section records each gate.

Noesis Ansible

The infrastructure side of Noesis. The agent stack defines and coordinates agent behavior; this repository provisions and configures the services it runs on: agent and MCP registries, policy and sandboxing, memory services, agent runtimes, and observability.

  • Phased, idempotent playbooks from host bootstrap to validation, with backup, restore, and rollback playbooks.
  • Targets in the repository today: local Docker hosts, macOS machines over a Tailscale tailnet, and SSH production inventories, plus Helm charts for Kubernetes and K3s.

I like building things that think. These days I'm working on Ora, GPT Researcher, Tavily and a few side projects.

Helps agents like OpenClaw find and learn new skills on their own.

A memory layer that helps AI agents give personal, context aware answers.

What I'm working on

  • Ora checks how well AI agents can find, read and use a website. Its open source tools are at github.com/ora, including ax, which scores agent readiness from your terminal or CI.
  • GPT Researcher is the open source deep research agent I created back in 2023, and it still has an active community to this day. The MCP server lets Claude, Cursor and other agents use it.
  • Tavily is the search engine for AI agents that I co-founded. The Python SDK is the easiest way to start using it.
  • Side projects include skyll, which helps agents learn new skills, and tovana, a memory layer for agents.

GPT Researcher

I started GPT Researcher in 2023 as the first open source deep research agent. You give it a question, it plans the research, reads dozens of sources in parallel and writes a report with citations. The community has kept improving it every week since.

To try it, start with the quickstart or install it from PyPI. You can also connect it to your own agent with the MCP server. Everything else is on gptr.dev and docs.gptr.dev, and you're welcome to say hi on Discord.

Cited in research

Carnegie Mellon's DeepResearchGym (May 2025) tested deep research systems on 1,000 complex questions. GPT Researcher came first, ahead of Perplexity, OpenAI, OpenDeepSearch and Hugging Face.
